body:
Current problem:
Cell Ontology currently has "articular chondrocyte" (CL:0002557) with only anatomical location-based children (knee joint, periarticular), but lacks terms for the well-established depth-dependent zones of articular cartilage. These zones have distinct molecular signatures, mechanical properties, and functions that are fundamental to cartilage biology and disease.

**Preferred term label**
1. superficial zone articular chondrocyte (or superficial zone chondrocyte)
2. middle zone articular chondrocyte (or transitional zone chondrocyte)
3. deep zone articular chondrocyte (or radial zone chondrocyte)
4. calcified zone articular chondrocyte

articular chondrocyte (CL:0002557)
├─ superficial zone articular chondrocyte (NEW)
├─ middle zone articular chondrocyte (NEW)
├─ deep zone articular chondrocyte (NEW)
├─ calcified zone articular chondrocyte (NEW)
├─ articular chondrocyte of knee joint (existing)
└─ periarticular chondrocyte (existing)

**Synonyms** (add reference(s), please)
provided with above terms

**Definition** (free text, with reference(s), please. PubMed ID format is PMID:XXXXXX)
PMID: 41226342 Histological and Immunohistochemical Methods in Normal and Osteoarthritic Knee Cartilage of Rat and Rabbit Models: A Literature Review
PMID: 18455690 Cartilage in normal and osteoarthritis conditions
PMID: 23124445 Zone-specific gene expression patterns in articular cartilage

Superficial zone articular chondrocyte:
An articular chondrocyte located in the most superficial layer of articular cartilage, characterized by flattened morphology, tangential alignment parallel to the joint surface, and high expression of lubricin (PRG4). These cells experience the highest shear stress and contain progenitor-like populations marked by CD44 and superficial zone protein.
Middle zone articular chondrocyte:
An articular chondrocyte located in the middle (transitional) zone of articular cartilage, characterized by round morphology, random spatial organization, and production of large amounts of proteoglycans and collagen. These cells represent the largest volume of articular cartilage and function primarily in load distribution.
Deep zone articular chondrocyte:
An articular chondrocyte located in the deep (radial) zone of articular cartilage, characterized by columnar arrangement perpendicular to the joint surface and high expression of collagen type X and MMP-13. These cells are in the highest proteoglycan concentration region and anchor to the calcified cartilage.
Calcified zone articular chondrocyte:
An articular chondrocyte located in the calcified cartilage zone at the interface between articular cartilage and subchondral bone, characterized by a hypertrophic-like phenotype, surrounded by calcified extracellular matrix, and expression of markers including collagen type X. This zone serves as a transitional interface providing mechanical integration between cartilage and bone.
